provenance.how: constructed from the ADR's literals at the pinned ref and cross-checked against the core's own builders (tests/unit/mobile/test_push_wire_contract.py); not captured from a running relay, because no relay route emits the machine-side shapes yet

notes: Idempotent on (install_id, platform): device_id and registered_at are STABLE across a re-register, and only the key (and the declarative metadata) is replaced — a device rotating its push token nightly cannot accumulate rows.

Q29: after a re-register the FIRST key no longer matches (device_key_matches is constant-time over the stored key), so the device_key shown here is the only live one. There is no 409 in this model — the key is stored as the key, not as a hash.
The device's own next authenticated register is the delivery path for a rotated key; the machine never pushes a key to a device.
A registration is REFUSED first when the row is revoked or unpaired, so this shape is only ever reached by a row that carries neither marker.
